title: Sukha Singh's Reputation, Domestic Return, and Excommunication

blocks.text: The narrative balances Sukha Singh's reputation for bravery with quieter camp virtues. He performs ordinary service, recites bani, remains prepared for combat, and thereby shows that Sikh heroism includes devotion and labor as well as battlefield prowess.

Family pressure nevertheless draws him back home long enough for marriage and domestic entanglement. After the death of an infant daughter, accusation and suspicion gather around him until he is ex-communicated by the Khalsa Panth and left in painful separation from the fellowship that defined him.
The page makes exclusion itself a form of torment. For a Singh formed by Panthic belonging, public disgrace wounds more deeply than bodily danger, setting up the need for a new proving ground.
